CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  October 3, 2022 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The regular meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 4:30 p.m.

CLOSED SESSION:  On the order of the Mayor, the meeting recessed at 4:33 p.m., to
  discuss the following closed session:

CLOSED SESSION  CITY COUNCIL CONSULTATION WITH INTERIM POLICE CHIEF
  JASON CLAWSON (PASADENA POLICE DEPARTMENT)
  REGARDING MATTERS RELATED TO THREATS TO PUBLIC
  SERVICES OR FACILITIES pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54957

  The above closed session item was discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:30 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Jones.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo, Councilmembers Madison, Hampton, Masuda, and
  Williams spoke on the passing of Dr. Ross Selvidge, whose voluntary
  service included the Pasadena representative on the Burbank-
  Glendale-Pasadena Airport Authority, where he was first appointed in
  2015 and served as Authority's President, Vice President and
  Secretary; member of the Planning Commission; member of the Rose
  Bowl Operating Company Board; and elected member to the
  Pasadena City College Trustee Board representing District 1. He was
  an advocate of the Pasadena Library system, and was an ardent
  community supporter in creating and later extending the voter-
  approved parcel tax that provides approximately 20% of the Pasadena
  library system's revenues. Mr. Selvidge served 27 years in the United
  States Navy, and was a long-time Pasadena resident that graduated

Council Minutes  10/03/2022
   from John Muir High School, attended PCC (where he was a gymnast
  and earned degrees in Architecture and Systems Management), and
  earned his Ph.D. in Finance at the University of San Diego. The City
  Council expressed their condolences to Dr. Ross Selvidge's family and
  friends, and requested that the meeting be adjourned in his memory.

  Interim Chief Clawson introduced and welcomed the new Sergeant-at-
  Arms, Sergeant Douglas Hamblin, and extended appreciation to
  Sergeant Joaquin Gurrola for his service.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring October 2021 as
  "National Disability Employment Awareness Month" in Pasadena. Ali
  Everett, Accessibility Coordinator, spoke on this important issues, and
  introduced Andrea Jennings, Accessibility & Disability Commission
  Chair, who thanked the Mayor and City Council for the proclamation
  and recognition and spoke on this year's theme "Disability: Part of the
  Equity Equation." Isis McDonald, Civitan President and Sr. Director of
  Business and Employment Services at AbilityFirst, provided
  information on their annual Hire Up Pasadena Civitan Employer
  Recognition event, to be held on October 13, 2022 at Villa Esperanza
  Service Campus. It was noted that Civitan Pasadena will also present
  the Servant's Heart Award to Assemblymember Chris Holden for his
  support of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation to Laura Rubio Cornejo,
  Director of Transportation, and members of Pasadena Complete
  Street Coalition and Day One, declaring October 2021 in Pasadena as
  "National Pedestrian Safety Month." Ms. Cornejo thanked the City
  Council for the recognition, and Day One and Pasadena Complete
  Streets Coalition for their partnership and collaboration. Ms. Cornejo
  invited the public to visit www.WalktoberPasadena.org and join in any
  of the Walktober events.

  Councilmember Wilson spoke on the importance of pedestrian safety;
  and expressed his thanks and appreciation to City staff, Pasadena
  Complete Streets, and Day One.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON  The following individuals spoke on the need for accountability and
MATTERS NOT ON THE  transparency within the Pasadena Police Department (PPD);
AGENDA  advocated for the termination of all Pasadena Police Officers involved
  in the shooting of Anthony McClain; expressed disappointment
  regarding the ongoing delay that has lasted two years for the PPD's
  Administrative Review, which has still not been completed:

  Michael Williams, Pasadena resident
  Brittney Pollock, Sherman Oaks resident
  Julia R, Los Angeles resident
  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident
  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident
  Adriana Bautista, Black Lives Matter - Pasadena

Council Minutes  2  10/03/2022
   The following individuals provided comments related to the application
  process for the City Council District 3 vacancy, expressed
  disappointment with the District 3 selection process, stating the
  peoples voices were overlooked and disregarded during this process:

  Anthony Manousos, Pasadena resident
  Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Dawn Burkhardt, Pasadena resident
  Kimberly Douglas, Pasadena resident
  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident
  Ed Washatka, Pasadena resident

  In response to questions raised by Councilmember Rivas regarding
  the planning for the next appointment process, the Mayor stated that
  the City Council will follow the process outlined in the City Charter, and
  he will provide the City Council with the timeline for that process.

  Councilmember Williams asked the City Manager and City Attorney to
  provide a timeline and/or information to the community on when,
  where (e.g. City Council meeting, Community Police Oversight
  Commission (CPOC)), and how the public can view and/or provide
  comments on the Administrative Review, the Office of Independent
  Review (OIR) report, and Independent Police Auditor (IPA) report
  concerning the office involved shooting incident of Anthony McClain.

  Recommendation: It is recommended that upon close of the public

  (1) Find that the recommended action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA
  Guidelines per Section 15061 (b)(3), the "common sense" provision

Council Minutes  8  10/03/2022
   assist low and moderate income individuals and families and address
  community development, affordable housing and homelessness
  needs.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, opened the public hearing; reported that the
  public hearing notice was published in the Pasadena Journal on
  September 29, 2022; and no correspondence was received by the City
  Clerk's Office on the matter.

  William Huang, Director of Housing, provided a brief summary of the
  agenda item; and responded to questions.

  Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident, expressed concern that the
  proposed action does not address objectives for reducing and
  ending homelessness; and advocated for general fund and
  America Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) be used for interim housing in
  the City.

  Jennifer O'Reilly-Jones, Program Coordinator Ill, responded to
  questions regarding the City's goals to address homeless matters, and
  provided additional information on the Homeless Overnight Shelter
  Program, weather-activated motel vouchers, and the Rapid
  Rehousing Programs.

  In response to Councilmember Williams questions related to
  opportunities to expand sources of funding for the programs in the
  coming years, William Huang, Director of Housing, stated that the
  funding comes directly from HUD, while stating there are some
  opportunities on the homeless services side to apply for some
  additional funding opportunities, noting that the Department is in the
  process of exploring those opportunities.

  Vice Mayor Wilson briefly commented on the Tiny Village Site Request
  for Information (RFI) process that is posted on the City's Plant Bids
  Website and anticipates further discussion on the matter.

  It was moved by Vice Mayor Wilson, seconded by Councilmember
  Williams to close the public hearing:

  Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo

  THE CITY COUNCIL, ALL OF ITS SUBORDINATE BODIES, AND
  ALL OF ITS NON-PROFIT CORPORATION BOARDS AND THEIR
  SUBORDINATE BODIES, TO MEET REMOTELY PURSUANT TO
  THE BROWN ACT
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action in the agenda report is exempt from review
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in
  accordance with State CEQA Guidelines Section 15061 (b)(3), the
  "common sense" exemption that CEQA only applies to projects that
  have the potential for causing a significant effect on the environment;
  and
  (2) Adopt A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Pasadena
  Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the City Council, all
  City subordinate bodies, and all City non-profit corporation Boards and
  their subordinate bodies, for the period October 3, 2022 through
  November 2, 2022. (Resolution No. 9953)

  Mayor Gordo expressed his support for the City Council to resume in-
  person City Council meetings.

  Councilmember Madison expressed his support to resume in-person
  meetings, but requested further information regarding opportunities for
  Councilmembers to continue to participate via video-conference
  technology (e.g. Zoom) when members are not be able to attend the
  meeting in-person (out of town, sick, etc.), noting that such
  participation would still comply with the Brown Act (post address on
  the agenda, allow public to participate at the remote location, etc.).

  Councilmember Hampton and Vice Mayor Wilson requested additional
  information regarding to allow the public to participate both remotely
  and in-person, noting the additional accessibility remote meeting
  participation provides to working families, and community members
  with disabilities.

  Following discussion, the City Council discussed options for hybrid
  meeting participation, which would allow the City Council and the
  public to attend meetings in the Council Chambers and others to
  attend virtually.

  In response to the City Council comments regarding hybrid meetings,
  the City Manager, City Attorney and City Clerk spoke on potential
  challenges, further resources and staffing that may be needed to
  conduct hybrid meetings, and noted that Councilmembers would have
  to be in-person unless remote participation complied with the Brown
  Act, and.
